packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Codex isolated image-only reader (model version not exposed)
text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Layout survey: image-001 shows a rectangular face bearing two visibly different scales of writing. Large dark text and square/diamond musical notes occupy broad horizontal bands ruled in orange-red. Much smaller brown prose is visible in two columns behind/between the musical material. The small writing appears interrupted or covered by the large notes and letters; this looks like superimposed writing rather than ordinary interlinear glossing. That is a visual interpretation, not a claim about date or origin. Several red paragraph marks belong to the smaller writing. The orange-red lines are musical ruling, not ordinary prose underlining. No securely readable running title or rubric. image-002 is an oblique spine/binding view; it shows only very narrow angled portions of the broad face, plus large shelf/label writing. It is not an independent full text page. I have not used the spine labels to identify anything.

Selected passage A: small right-column prose in the upper part of image-001. Physical line numbers below refer to derived crop-b.jpg, counted from its top; large notes are excluded from the line count.
crop-b.jpg L1: [upper part cut] [illegible]
crop-b.jpg L2: Non? dampna? hic [illegible]
crop-b.jpg L3: [left cut] am? [illegible] precepto? [illegible]
crop-b.jpg L4: de servitute hic ultimo loco posuit
crop-b.jpg L5: etiam? [illegible] tua? [illegible]

Selected passage B: small right-column prose farther down image-001. Physical lines refer to crop-a.jpg, counted from its top; this crop does not repeat passage A.
crop-a.jpg L1: [illegible]
crop-a.jpg L2: [illegible]
crop-a.jpg L3: scilicet? in ea condicione? [illegible] exem-
crop-a.jpg L4: plo. Ut? enim [illegible] ita [illegible]
crop-a.jpg L5: et [illegible] esse? potest [illegible]

Separate large musical-text layer, image-001.jpg: The large letters are visible but several are cut or worn. I do not supply a joined reading from the isolated surviving word-parts. This layer has not been conflated with the small prose above.

Coverage and limitations: Both full images were surveyed. Only two short consecutive runs of the small right-column text are reported; even these contain considerable uncertainty. The clearest phrase is the fourth line of crop-b. The left small-text column, the rest of the right column, and the musical words remain untranscribed. The lower-right prose was additionally examined in crop-c but did not yield a sufficiently secure new connected passage. Underlying letters disappear at the musical notes and ruling. There is no basis here to supply their missing words. No individual deletion or insertion is securely distinguishable from the superimposed layers. A flat view of the other broad face, and imaging capable of separating the layers, would be useful.

Transforms: image-001 is 4912 x 7360 pixels. crop-a = fractional rectangle x=.44–.81, y=.28–.40, resized to 1480 x 960; crop-b = x=.44–.82, y=.12–.24, resized to 1480 x 960; crop-c = x=.445–.81, y=.425–.558, native crop. No rotation or contrast changes. Crops are derived views, not additional manuscript text. No outside sources, catalogue, or candidate identification consulted.
